title: Uniform exponential moments for first-exit particles of nondegenerate critical branching random walks with exponential offspring moments
author: Amine Asselah; Bruno Schapira
work: Time spent in a ball by a critical branching random walk
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.281
difficulty_reason: A BGW exponential-moment bound by itself does not control the number of particles frozen at a spatial boundary, because repeated interior generations and spatial displacement remain coupled. The authors first contract the killed tree in generation blocks, then construct a quadratic spatial martingale linking its occupation to the frozen boundary population and control that martingale with the new killed-occupation estimate. The exit-probability and exponential-expansion steps then give the uniform squared-radius and sharper interior-start assertions, beyond standard BGW and random-walk prerequisites.
